In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period.﴾

Tafsir of Surat al-Talaq

It is Medinan, according to the consensus of all.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾. If it is said: How does He address the Prophet alone at the beginning and then say, ﴿when you divorce women﴾? The answer has several aspects. The first: the address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to his community, like the address of a leader being an address to his followers; as if He had said: O Prophet and believers, when you divorce women.

The second answer: His saying, ﴿when you divorce women﴾, is a shift of the address to a third party, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it...﴾.

The third answer: there is an omitted element in it, and its implied meaning is: O Prophet, say to the believers, when you divorce women. Qatadah narrated from Anas that the Prophet divorced Hafsah, so Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse, and Jibril said to him: Your Lord says to you: take her back, for she is one who fasts much and stands in prayer much, and she is among your wives in Paradise.

His saying: ﴿so divorce them at their waiting period﴾ means: at the time of their waiting period, which is the state of purity (ṭuhr). In it there is evidence that the qurʾ (qurū'), by which the waiting period is completed, are the periods of purity, and this is the view of the people of the Hijaz. As for the one who said that the qurū' are menstruation, he said the meaning of His saying ﴿at their waiting period﴾ is: that they may observe the waiting period, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾, that is, that they might grieve; this was mentioned by al-Naḥḥas. In an irregular reading (shādh) it is recited: "divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period (li-qubul ʿiddatihinna)." It is said that this is the recitation of the Prophet. Whoever says that the qurū' are menstruation takes evidence from this recitation, because this wording requires that the time of divorce be before ﴿and count the waiting period and fear Allah, your Lord﴾, the time of the waiting period, and that the time of the waiting period follows the time of divorce.

As for the one who said that the qurū' are the periods of purity, he said the meaning of His saying "at the beginning of their waiting period" is: at the front of their waiting period; for it is said that the beginning of a thing is its front. And the intended meaning is the very beginning of the period of purity. If it is said: the beginning and the end of the period of purity are one in respect of divorce, so the meaning is nothing other than what we have mentioned.

We say: it is not so; rather, it is better to divorce at the very beginning of the period of purity when one intends divorce, because if he delays, he cannot be sure that he will not have intercourse with her and then divorce, and so he would have divorced in the manner of innovation (bid'ah).

It has been related from ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and others among the Successors that the meaning of His saying ﴿at their waiting period﴾ is: in a state of purity without intercourse. This wording has also been established from the Prophet, through the narration of Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, that he divorced his wife during menstruation, so the Prophet said to him: "Take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure; then if you wish, divorce her while she is pure, without intercourse." That is the waiting period by which Allah, Exalted is He, commanded that women be divorced. In another narration: he said to ʿUmar: "Order him to take her back." In another narration: "Then when she becomes pure, if he wishes, let him divorce her while she is pure, without intercourse," and it does not mention "then she menstruates, then becomes pure." It is related from Anas and Ibn Sirin that they said to Ibn ʿUmar: "Did you count that single divorce?" He said: "Yes." (In another narration: five.) In a third narration he said: "Yes, even if you were incapable and acted foolishly."

His saying ﴿and count the waiting period﴾ is an address to the husbands; He commanded them to count the waiting period so that they would know the time of return (ruj'ah) and the length of its cessation. It is also said: so that they would know the length of maintenance owed to them.

His saying ﴿and fear Allah, your Lord﴾ means: divorce in accordance with the Sunnah, and do not divorce in innovation. It is also said: fear your Lord regarding not expelling them from the houses. As for the manner of the divorce of the Sunnah, in terms of time, it is that ﴿do not expel them from their houses, nor should they go out unless they commit a clear immorality﴾; he divorces her while she is pure, without intercourse. As for its manner in terms of the waiting period: the school of Malik, al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah and many scholars hold that it is disliked to divorce three times at once, and the Sunnah is to divorce her once and leave her until her waiting period ends; this is the preferred course, as stated by Malik. If he wishes to divorce three times, he separates them over periods of purity, divorcing once for each purity. As for the school of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, there is neither Sunnah nor innovation in combining or separating. The companions (al-aṣḥab) have mentioned that the preferred course is to divorce once, although combining the three is not considered disliked; they said: and this is the school's position. In the verse there is evidence (for al-Shafiʿi) for his view, because Allah, Exalted is He, permitted divorce by His saying ﴿so divorce them at their waiting period﴾ unrestrictedly, and did not distinguish between divorcing one or more; and because Allah, Exalted is He, specified the time of divorce and did not specify its number, and the verse came to explain the prescribed form of divorce; so if there were a Sunnah in the number of divorces, its explanation would not have been delayed.

His saying ﴿do not expel them from their houses﴾ means: during the waiting period; and the houses are attributed to them because of residence.

His saying ﴿nor should they go out﴾ means: they should not leave on their own.

His saying ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: opinions differ on the meaning of "immorality" (fāḥishah) here. The most apparent opinion is that it is fornication (zinā); this is the view of Ibn Masʿud, one of two narrations from Ibn ʿAbbas, and the view of al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbi, ʿIkrimah, Ḥammad ibn Abi Salamah, al-Layth and a large group. On this view, the meaning of the verse is: unless she commits fornication and so goes out to have the prescribed punishment established.

The second opinion: the immorality is that she behaves abusively toward her family (tabdhū ʿalā ahlihā). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas in one of two narrations, and it is said that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is: "unless they behave immorally (yafḥishna)," and this reading strengthens this view. It is narrated from ʿAʾishah that she said to Fatimah bint Qays: "Fear Allah, for you know that the Messenger expelled you," meaning from the house of her husband, and she used to be abusive with her tongue.

The third opinion is what is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, that he said: the immorality is the very act of going out. It is reported from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi. On this view, the sense of the verse is: unless they commit a clear immorality by going out.

Some of them said: the immorality here is all acts of disobedience. The most preferred of these opinions is the first, because of the large number who held it, and because it agrees with His saying ﴿and those of your women who commit immorality﴾, and they are agreed that what is meant there is fornication.

His saying ﴿and those are the limits of Allah﴾: al-Suddi said: they are the conditions of Allah. It is also said: the law of Allah; and it was said: His command and His prohibition.

His saying ﴿and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself﴾ means: he has destroyed himself and brought ruin upon it.

His saying ﴿you do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: the well-known view regarding this is that it is the desire for reconciliation (murājaʿah). In it there is evidence that what is meant by His saying at the beginning of the verse, ﴿divorce them﴾, is one divorce or two divorces, not three. It is also said that what is meant by it is one and three together. Regarding His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿you do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾, he said: it is abrogation (naskh); its meaning: perhaps Allah will abrogate this ruling and lift it. And it was said: it is the desire to begin a marriage after another husband.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 2:

And His words: ﴿Then when they reach their term﴾ mean: they are about to reach the end of their term, which is the completion of the waiting period (ʿidda).

And His words: ﴿then retain them in kindness﴾ mean: take them back in kindness, and its meaning is: in accordance with the command of Allah the Exalted. It is said: the kindness here is that he takes her back in order to keep her, not that he takes her back only to divorce her again, so that he prolongs the waiting period against her, as the people of the Jahiliyya used to do.

And His words: ﴿or part from them in kindness﴾ mean: that he leaves her so that the waiting period comes to an end and separation takes place. And "kindness" is what Allah the Exalted has commanded of delivering her rights to her, namely housing and maintenance, in the place where they are obligatory. It is also said: "in kindness" means: without intending to harm her.

As for His words: ﴿and call to witness two just men from among you﴾, there are three opinions concerning it. The first: that calling witnesses is obligatory in both divorce and taking back, according to the apparent meaning of the verse.

The second opinion: that calling witnesses is obligatory in taking back but not obligatory in separation; this is one of the two opinions of al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him), and it is the view of Tawus from among the Successors.

The third opinion: that calling witnesses is recommended (mandub) in taking back and not obligatory; most of the scholars hold this view, and it is the other opinion of al-Shafiʿi (may Allah have mercy on him).

As for "just" (ʿadl), it is one whose condition is upright in dealings and commands of the Sharia. Mansur said: I asked Ibrahim about the just person, and he said: it is the one in whom no suspicion has appeared.

And His words: ﴿and establish testimony for Allah﴾ are an address to the witnesses to render the testimonies in their proper forms.

And His words: ﴿This is what is admonished to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾.

And His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: from every matter that is difficult for people. And from him he said: if he fears Allah regarding divorce in the manner of the Sunna, by divorcing once, He will make for him a way out of it through the permissibility of taking back. It is narrated that a man came to him and said: "My uncle divorced his wife three times; is there a way out for him?" He said: "Your uncle disobeyed Allah and sinned, and obeyed Satan, so He did not make for him a way out." And in some reports, through the narration of Ibn ʿAbbas, the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning His words: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾: "[It is] from the griefs of this world, the agonies of death, and the hardships of the Hereafter."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, meaning: from where he does not hope or anticipate. It was also said: He makes him content with what He has provided him. In the tafsir (exegesis) it is related: "This verse was revealed concerning ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, whose son was taken captive. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) complaining to him, and he said: 'Be patient and fear Allah.' So he returned. Then the enemy became heedless of his son once, and he fled from them and drove with himself camels, and returned to his father and brought the camels. He came to the Prophet and informed him of that, and asked him whether it was lawful for him to have what his son had driven to him. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse." Thus the meaning of His saying ﴿And provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ is what Ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik brought to his father of the camels.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾, meaning: he places his trust in Allah and entrusts his affair to Him. It is also said: reliance upon Allah is contentment with His decree. And in some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is stated that he said: "Whoever devotes himself to Allah, Allah will suffice him for every burden, and whoever devotes himself to creation, He will leave him to them."

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾, meaning: whatever He wills concerning His creation.

And His saying: ﴿Allah has already set for everything a decree﴾, meaning: a measure and a term at which it ends.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾, the verse is problematic in relation to His saying: ﴿if you are in doubt﴾. The opinions differ concerning His saying: ﴿if you are in doubt﴾. The most evident of the opinions is that when Allah, exalted is He, explained the waiting period of women who have menstrual cycles (qurū', sing. qar', a term meaning both menstruation and purity), a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah said: "We have known the waiting period of those with menstrual cycles, but what is the waiting period of those who have despaired (of menstruation), of the young girls, and of those who are pregnant?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ is addressed to that group, meaning: you have become uncertain about their waiting period and so you did not know it. In some of the exegetical reports: Umm Mu'adh ibn Jabal asked the Messenger of Allah about this. And it is related from some of them that Ubayy ibn Ka'b asked the Messenger of Allah about this.

The second opinion: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ means: you did not know whether she menstruates or does not menstruate, and this concerns a young woman whose menstruation has stopped due to a cause. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: she should wait seven months; if she does not see menstruation, she observes a waiting period of three months. This is the view of Malik, and it is related from Mujāhid something similar to what we have mentioned.

The third opinion: His saying, ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ refers back to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave﴾, and the meaning is: if you are in doubt about the end of her waiting period, then do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave. This was mentioned by al-Naḥḥās. As for the one who has despaired (āyisa), she is the one whose peers no longer see menstruation, so her waiting period is three months. According to the position of most scholars, a young woman whose menstruation has stopped due to a cause does not complete her waiting period by months as long as she has not despaired; they said: had Allah willed, He would have tested her with more than that.

His saying: ﴿and those who have not menstruated﴾ are the young girls (ṣaghā'ir).

His saying: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾. This ruling is agreed upon concerning pregnant divorcees. As for the widow, the Companions differed on this: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās said: her waiting period is the farther of the two terms. ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar and Abū Hurayrah said: her waiting period is by the delivery of the child, and this is the preferred view. It is related from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: Sūrat al-Nisā' al-Quṣrā (the short Sūrat al-Nisā') was revealed after His saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives﴾, so Ibn Masʿūd transmitted the abrogation of that verse by this verse. In another report from him he said: this verse abrogates that verse. It is also narrated that Abū Hurayrah and Ibn ʿAbbās differed on this matter: Ibn ʿAbbās said: she observes the farther of the two terms, and Abū Hurayrah said: she observes it by the delivery of the child. So Ibn ʿAbbās sent Kurayb, his freedman, to Umm Salamah to ask her about this, and she related that Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah's husband died while she was pregnant, and she delivered within half a month; she asked the Messenger of Allah about this and he said: "You are free to marry." This is a sound report.

His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair﴾, meaning: whoever fears Allah regarding the matter of divorce, seeking what is in accordance with the Sunnah.

His saying: ﴿He will make for him ease in his affair﴾, meaning: the return (to the wife, i.e. ruj'ah). Some have said: "whoever fears Allah" means he guards against sins and acts in obedience, "He will make for him ease in his affair" means He grants him success, guides him, and makes matters easy for him.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you﴾, i.e., what preceded of the command and prohibition concerning divorce and its rulings.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and will make his reward great﴾, i.e., on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 6:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾. The scholars differed concerning the obligation of residence (al-sukna) for the woman irrevocably divorced (al-mabtuta), although they agreed that it is obligatory for the woman who may be revoked (al-raj'iyya). The position of al-Shafi'i is that residence is obligatory for her but maintenance (al-nafaqa) is not, except for the pregnant woman, for whom both maintenance and residence are obligatory; this is also the view of Malik.

﴿...according to your means, and do not harm them so as to constrict them. And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they deliver their burden. And if they nurse for you, then give them their payment﴾. The position of Ahmad and a group of scholars is that residence and maintenance are not obligatory for the irrevocably divorced woman, on the basis of the hadith of Fatima bint Qays. The position of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, is that both are obligatory.

His words ﴿according to your means﴾ mean: according to your capacity (sa'ah). Al-Farra' said: "from what you find (tajidun)." Al-A'raj recited "min wujdikum," which is a lahn (a mistake in recitation), because wujd (means) is from wajd (ecstasy/feeling), while jadd (wealth/fortune) is from grief, longing and tenderness, and this is not the place for it.

His words: ﴿And do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾. Mansur related from Abu al-Duha: harm (al-mudarra) is that he takes her back at the moment she is about to complete the waiting period (al-'idda), without desire for her, so as to prolong the waiting period upon her. It is said that the intended harm here is harm in the dwelling and residence; this was said by Mujahid.

His words: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend upon them until they deliver their burden﴾.

Whoever does not require maintenance for the pregnant irrevocably divorced woman argued from this verse, saying that Allah, the Exalted, made the obligation of maintenance for irrevocably divorced women conditional upon their being pregnant. Whoever requires maintenance for them said: His words ﴿and do not harm them so as to constrict them﴾ mean: by withholding maintenance, in general, from the irrevocably divorced women.

His words ﴿And if they are pregnant﴾ are a specification of part of what the first wording covered, mentioned explicitly, like His words ﴿and Gabriel and Michael﴾ after the mention of the angels. Some of them said: the verse is to explain the duration of maintenance, meaning that maintenance is obligatory for the pregnant woman however long her pregnancy lasts, until she delivers the child.

His words ﴿And if they nurse for you, then give them their payment﴾ mean: if the mother nurses after the divorce, the father gives her her wage.

His words ﴿And confer among yourselves with kindness﴾ mean: let the father and the mother agree upon what is most beneficial for the child, so that the mother does not refuse to nurse and the father does not refuse to give the wage. Al-Suddi said: "And confer (ta'tamiru) among yourselves with kindness" means: consult one another with kindness. This is a weak view. Al-Mubarrad said: let some of you command others with kindness.

His words ﴿And if you disagree﴾ mean: you are straitened and dispute over the wage.

His words ﴿then another woman shall nurse for him﴾ mean: if the mother does not agree to the standard wage (ajr al-mithl) and asks for more, the child is handed over to another woman to nurse for the standard wage.

His words ﴿then another woman shall nurse for him﴾ are an informative statement with the meaning of a command, i.e., "let her nurse," like His words ﴿And the mothers nurse their children﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿Let the one of wide means spend from his wealth﴾ means: in proportion to his wealth. It is an exhortation to be generous in spending for the one whom Allah has granted abundance.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted for him﴾ means: his provision was constricted for him, and he had nothing except sustenance (al-qut) and what resembles it. And this is His saying: ﴿let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, meaning: according to that measure.

It is related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard that Abu ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrah wore coarse clothing and ate rough food (al-jashab). So he sent to him a thousand dinars from the treasury (bayt al-mal), and he ordered the messenger to observe his condition afterward. Abu ʿUbayda then became more generous, ate good food, and wore soft garments. The messenger returned and informed ʿUmar of this, and he said: "He has interpreted the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Let the one of wide means spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted for him, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾." Mentioned by al-Qaffal in his tafsir.

And His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾ and His saying: ﴿Allah will bring about ease after hardship﴾, meaning: after constriction comes abundance, and after poverty comes wealth. The people of tafsir said: it refers to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who were in hardship, then Allah granted them abundance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 8:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾ mean: its people transgressed against the command of their Lord. Ataw (rebellion) is excessiveness in disobedience.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that Allah the Most High did not send down any drop from the sky except by a known measure, except in the time of Nuh, and He does not send any wind except by a known measure, except in the time of 'Ad, for it rebelled against its keepers (khazzan).

And His words: ﴿So We called it to account with a severe reckoning﴾: the severe reckoning is that in which there is no pardon and no overlooking.

And His words: ﴿And We punished it with a terrible punishment﴾: i.e., one that is denounced (yunkar), and the munkar (dreadful) is that which is hideous.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So she tasted the evil consequence of her affair﴾, meaning: the outcome of her affair in what is disliked. It is said: "A wabil (harmful) food," meaning disliked, which is the opposite of hani' (wholesome, pleasant) food. And it is said: wabil food is that whose consequence leads to destruction.

And His saying: ﴿And it was the outcome of their affair a loss﴾, meaning: destruction. It was also said: decrease (loss).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 10:

And His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment﴾, which is the Fire.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So fear Allah, O you of understanding (ulu al-albab)﴾, meaning: the people of intellect (ulu al-'uqul) who have believed. This indicates that intellect benefits only together with faith, and that without faith it does not benefit.

And His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly sent down to you a reminder, a messenger﴾. In this there are several views. The first: "He has sent down to you a reminder," meaning a proof (dalil), "and He has sent down a messenger." It is said: the reminder (al-dhikr) is the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 11:

His words, ﴿a Messenger﴾, are in the accusative as a substitution (badal). It is also said that "a Messenger" means a message (risalah), so the meaning is: He sent down the Qur'an as a message.

His words, ﴿reciting﴾: it is said that this refers to Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is said that it refers to Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him.

His words, ﴿clear signs upon you﴾, mean: manifest and evident.

His words, ﴿that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darknesses into light﴾, mean: from disbelief (kufr) to faith (iman), and from falsehood (batil) to truth (haqq), and what is similar to that.

His words, ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision﴾, mean: Paradise (al-Jannah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 65, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens, and of the earth the like thereof﴾. There is no verse in the Qur'an that indicates the number of the earths as seven, like the number of the heavens, other than this verse. It is also established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever usurps a span of land, Allah will collar him with it from seven earths."

And from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: The seven heavens are above one another, and the seven earths are beneath one another, and between each heaven and heaven is a distance of five hundred years, and likewise between each earth and earth. And from him, he said: The lowest heaven was created from a restrained wave, the second heaven from a rock, the third heaven from iron, the fourth from copper, the fifth from silver, the sixth from gold, and the seventh from a pearl. And He created the Kursi (Footstool) above the heavens and the earth; in comparison to the Kursi it is like a ring in a desert. And the Kursi is carried by four angels, each angel having four faces: one face in the form of the children of Adam, asking for provision for mankind; one face in the form of the lord of beasts of prey, which is the lion, asking for provision for the beasts of prey; one face in the form of the lord of birds, which is the eagle, asking for provision for the birds; and one face in the form of the lord of livestock, which is the bull, asking for provision for livestock.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Ever since the calf was worshipped besides Allah, there has been a stain on the face that is in the form of the bull. So one angel says: "O Allah, to You belongs praise for Your bearing after Your knowledge," and another angel says: "O Allah, to You belongs praise for Your pardon after Your power."

And from him, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: In every earth there is an Adam like the father of mankind, and a Noah like Noah, and an Abraham like Abraham, and a Moses like Moses, and a Jesus like Jesus, and a Muhammad like Muhammad. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Naqqash mentioned these reports from Ibn 'Abbas in his tafsir. And from Qatadah, he said: In every heaven and in every earth there is a creation of His creation, a command of His command, and a decree of His decree.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The command descends between them﴾, that is, between the heavens and the earths, and this is the meaning of what we have explained.

His saying: ﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent﴾, that is, capable.

His saying: ﴿And that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾, the meaning is apparent, and it is in the accusative case as a tamyiz (specification), and Allah knows best.
